current_sources: PDF and SVG can contain raster images. This dialog disables resolution editing for these formats.
Line colour affects axes spines and tick marks in Matplotlib exports; fast plots also recolour plotted lines.
Line width applies only to fast-plot exports, in pixels. Matplotlib exports keep their existing line widths.
Text colour affects axes titles, labels, tick labels, legend entries and axes annotations. Matplotlib figure titles and legend titles keep their existing colours.
Resolution in dots per inch for PNG and TIFF exports.
This figure cannot be previewed. It will be saved using its current styling, the selected resolution and background transparency, and a tight crop.
retired_sources: PDF and SVG are true vector: the page size is the whole answer and there is no resolution to set
Every line in the file: the plotted curves, the reference lines, the axis spines and the tick marks. The numbers beside the ticks are text and follow the text colour.
Pen width in pixels for every line. A line that reads well on screen is often too thin once the figure is a column wide.
Every piece of text in the file: the title, the axis labels, the numbers beside the ticks and the legend.
Dots per inch in the written file. 300 is the usual journal minimum; the screen never needs more than about 150.
This figure cannot be previewed, so it will be written exactly as it appears on screen.
